chapter: Learning the drums and first job
title: His early drum set: cowbells, cymbals, overhead beater
summary: He describes his full set with four cowbells, Chinese and Turkish cymbals and the old overhead beater.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did you have a full set of drums when you started? I did. You got bass drum and snare. Yeah, bass drum and everything.
Snairs, cowbells, cymbals and everything.
How many cowbells did you use in those days? Four.
Yeah.
Albert Giles had a set of four of them. Yeah, he did. I remember Baby Dodds had a set of four in Chicago. I always saw his. Yeah. And what kind of cymbals did you use?
I had one large crash cymbal and then I had a... Was that the Chinese one?
Yeah. That turned up on the edges and all that? Right, yeah. That's it.
Made in the Chinese style. Yeah. Mm-hmm.
And then another, was it a Turkish cymbal, regular? Yeah, I had a Turkish cymbal.
Yeah.
That's true. When you started, did you have one of those cymbals down on the drum that the pedal would get there? Yeah, we did.
It was an overhead beater we had first. Yeah. You had the overhead beater. Yeah.
And then after, then the flow beater come in style. Yeah. And I used both.
I worked on both of them.
Yeah. You hadn't had one of those old overhead beaters anymore? No.
I wish I could get one.
That thing is... Yeah. That's right, yeah. You don't know anybody that has one around, I guess.
No, I wish I would.
I guess everybody threw them out when they bought their good pedals. It would be nice to have one now to see how they work.
Uh-huh.
